lanes.title: What a vision model can read off a spectrogram

findings.title: Vision Language Models Are Few-Shot Audio Spectrogram Classifiers
findings.finding: GPT-4o on labelled spectrogram images scored 59.0% on ESC-10 vs Gemini-1.5 native audio 49.6%, matching human spectrogram readers (73.75 vs 72.5 on fold 1).
findings.implication: The image is a real channel at coarse-category resolution; never a gate.

findings.title: Vision Language Models Are Few-Shot Audio Spectrogram Classifiers (ablation)
findings.finding: Ablation (default render = viridis, log frequency, log amplitude, axis labels on, colorbar off -> 27.5% zero-shot): linear frequency axis best (35.0%), linear amplitude 30.0%; magma (25.0%), mel (25.0%), showing a colorbar (23.75%), removing labels (26.25%), low resolution (20.0%) and MFCCs (13.75%) all below the default; few-shot exemplars lifted GPT-4o to 70-76%.
findings.implication: Keep axis labels, no colorbar, expose frequency scale and colormap as parameters, ship labelled exemplar plates; neither the MIR-default log render nor magma is automatically best for a VLM.

findings.title: Seeing isn't Hearing: Benchmarking Vision Language Models at Interpreting Spectrograms
findings.finding: Open VLMs read fine-grained speech content off spectrograms at chance (25%); phonetician 75%, ASR 87.6%; adding a waveform did not help.
findings.implication: The 50-cent and 40-ms gates never route through the image.

findings.title: Evaluating few-shot prompting for spectrogram-based lung sound classification using a multimodal language model
findings.finding: GPT-4o on real clinical mel spectrograms: 32.0% zero-shot, 36.3% few-shot vs 25% chance.
findings.implication: Budget the surface as orientation, not measurement.

findings.title: CaReCoS: A Spectrogram based Visual Benchmark for Cardiac, Respiratory and Cough Sounds
findings.finding: Best of nine current vision/omni models scored 51.2% on mel-spectrogram QA; none combined visual pattern recognition with domain knowledge reliably.
findings.implication: Pair the image with a text block of extracted features; domain knowledge is supplied, not assumed.

findings.title: PitchBench: Measuring Pitch Hearing in Audio-Language Models
findings.finding: Audio-language models score 8-48% on pitch across 28 experiments, chords under 20%, and shift with notation (SPN good, Hz bad).
findings.implication: Pitch belongs to DSP; when the model states pitch, use note names, never Hz.

findings.title: A Picture is Worth A Thousand Numbers: Enabling LLMs Reason about Time Series via Visualization
findings.finding: Rendering a numeric series as an image instead of dumping numbers improved LLM reasoning ~140% and cut tokens ~99%.
findings.implication: Return image + compact numbers, never the raw frame matrix.

findings.title: DEAF: A Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of Acoustic Faithfulness in Audio Language Models
findings.finding: Audio multimodal model predictions are driven mainly by text input even when acoustics contradict it.
findings.implication: Blind the critic: describe the render before seeing the intended notes.

findings.title: CharXiv: Charting Gaps in Realistic Chart Understanding in Multimodal LLMs
findings.finding: GPT-4o reads realistic charts at 47.1% vs humans 80.5%.
findings.implication: Reading precise values off any plotted axis has a general ceiling.

findings.title: SonicBench: Dissecting the Physical Perception Bottleneck in Large Audio Language Models
findings.finding: Large audio-language models are strong on semantics but unreliable on pitch, timing, loudness and duration.
findings.implication: The picture localises; it never measures.

findings.title: Deep Salience Representations for F0 Estimation in Polyphonic Music
findings.finding: HCQT: 60 bins/octave (20 cents), 11 ms hop, fmin C1 32.7 Hz, 6 octaves, harmonics {0.5,1,2,3,4,5} stacked.
findings.implication: At 20 cents/bin a 50-cent error spans 2.5 bins and is visible without overlay.

findings.title: A Lightweight Instrument-Agnostic Model for Polyphonic Note Transcription and Multipitch Estimation
findings.finding: Basic Pitch uses a CQT at 3 bins/semitone, ~11 ms hop, 7 harmonics + 1 sub-harmonic, scored under MIREX quarter-tone / 50 ms rules.
findings.implication: 36 bins/octave is the proven floor for note-level work; 60 is the pitch-gate resolution.

findings.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
findings.finding: Whisper's input is an 80-channel log-mel at 16 kHz, 25 ms window, 10 ms stride.
findings.implication: Log-mel at ~10 ms hop is what LLM-adjacent audio models are trained on: the legibility surface, not the measurement surface.

findings.title: AST: Audio Spectrogram Transformer
findings.finding: AST reaches 0.485 mAP on AudioSet from 128-bin log-mel, 25 ms Hamming, 10 ms shift.
findings.implication: 25 ms / 10 ms / 80-128 mel is the de facto standard for what the model hears.

findings.title: Onsets and Frames: Dual-Objective Piano Transcription
findings.finding: SOTA piano transcription ran on 229 log-mel bins (16 kHz, n_fft 2048, hop 512), note F1 82.3 at 50 ms.
findings.implication: Mel with many bins is sufficient for onsets and note identity on piano; use 229, not the speech default.

findings.title: Improved Musical Onset Detection with Convolutional Neural Networks
findings.finding: Three stacked log-mels (23/46/93 ms windows, 10 ms hop, 80 bands) reached F 88.5-89.9% at a 25 ms tolerance.
findings.implication: A 10 ms hop clears the 40 ms gate with 4x margin; a short-window channel sharpens onsets.

findings.title: Auditory Toolbox - mel_frequencies
findings.finding: Slaney mel is linear below 1 kHz at 200/3 = 66.7 Hz per step, so a 50-cent error at C4 (7.7 Hz) is one-ninth of a filter spacing.
findings.implication: Mel alone cannot show the 50-cent gate in the vocal/guitar fundamental range: the decisive argument for a CQT primary.

findings.title: CREPE: A Convolutional Representation for Pitch Estimation
findings.finding: CREPE raw pitch accuracy 0.967 at 50 cents and 0.909 at 10 cents vs pYIN 0.919 / 0.826.
findings.implication: Overlay a tracker's f0 in cents-vs-target on the CQT; the picture shows why, the tracker supplies the number.

findings.title: MERT: Acoustic Music Understanding Model with Large-Scale Self-supervised Training
findings.finding: MERT adds a CQT musical teacher beside its codec acoustic teacher to model pitched structure.
findings.implication: Even mel/codec music models bolt a CQT back on for pitch; corroborates a two-surface design.

lanes.title: How to draw it so a vision model can read it

findings.title: librosa.display.cmap / specshow (0.11)
findings.finding: librosa's canonical sequential colormap for dB-scaled data is magma.
findings.implication: Magma is the MIR convention, but the one VLM measurement (finding 2) scored it below viridis: viridis default, magma alternate, both exposed.

findings.title: librosa.amplitude_to_db (0.11)
findings.finding: amplitude_to_db defaults to ref=1.0, top_db=80, thresholding 80 dB below the peak.
findings.implication: Clip 80 dB below peak and normalise per image.

findings.title: Sonic Visualiser: A Brief Reference (4.5) - log-frequency spectrogram axis
findings.finding: The log-frequency spectrogram replaces the numeric y-axis with a stylised piano keyboard, every octave's C shaded.
findings.implication: Draw a keyboard strip with C shading instead of Hz ticks.

findings.title: Sonic Visualiser: A Brief Reference (4.5) - layers
findings.finding: Layers stack like a graphics application: spectrogram at the back, notes and onsets in front.
findings.implication: Overlaying the piano roll and beat grid on the spectrogram is the established MIR idiom.

findings.title: Acoustic spectral feedback in vocal learning: a systematic review of psychological mechanisms and skill outcomes
findings.finding: Spectrogram displays for vocal learning are thinly evidenced next to simple pitch-trajectory displays; recommended as auxiliary observation, not standalone instruction.
findings.implication: Always pair the spectrogram with a pitch-contour-vs-target line.

findings.title: Vision - developer documentation
findings.finding: Claude reads images as 28x28-px patches, caps standard models at 1568 px long edge, and warns resizing can make text less legible.
findings.implication: Render at exactly 1568 px wide; give a semitone whole patch rows.

findings.title: Images and vision - API guide
findings.finding: High-detail pipeline scales the short edge down to 768 px before tiling at 512 px.
findings.implication: Budget legibility against a 768-px-high render; keep the aspect wide-and-short.

findings.title: Vision language models are blind
findings.finding: Four SOTA VLMs average 58% on overlapping primitives but reach near-100% when marks are separated by space.
findings.implication: The score overlay must be hollow, offset, never superimposed on the harmonic band.

findings.title: riffusion spectrogram_params.py
findings.finding: Riffusion encodes 512 HTK-mel bins to 10 kHz, 10 ms hop, power exponent 0.25, and stores render parameters in PNG EXIF.
findings.implication: Emit render parameters as a sidecar; a ^0.25 map is a proven alternative to dB clipping.

lanes.title: What a spectrogram can honestly measure

findings.title: Frechet Audio Distance: A Metric for Evaluating Music Enhancement Algorithms
findings.finding: Magnitude L2 correlated -0.01 and cosine -0.15 with human ratings; FAD 0.52.
findings.implication: Never surface log-mel L1/L2 as a quality number; label it a deviation diagnostic.

findings.title: Correlation of Frechet Audio Distance With Human Perception of Environmental Audio Is Embedding Dependant
findings.finding: FAD's human agreement exceeds Spearman 0.5 with PANNs-WGM-LogMel and falls below 0.1 with VGGish.
findings.implication: If FAD ever ships, pin and name the embedding.

findings.title: A Survey on Evaluation Metrics for Music Generation
findings.finding: FAD is distributional and needs large reference sets; CLAP measures prompt relevance; both align poorly with human preference.
findings.implication: Exclude FAD and CLAP from any single-take tool.

findings.title: mir_eval: A Transparent Implementation of Common MIR Metrics
findings.finding: mir_eval defaults encode 50 ms onset and 50 cent pitch tolerance.
findings.implication: The 40 ms gate is stricter than convention; report the 50 ms figure alongside.

findings.title: Maximum Filter Vibrato Suppression for Onset Detection
findings.finding: SuperFlux's maximum filter over spectral trajectories cuts onset false positives up to 60% on vibrato-heavy material.
findings.implication: Use SuperFlux, not plain spectral flux, on the singing route.

findings.title: Chirp Group Delay based Onset Detection in Instruments with Fast Attack
findings.finding: SOTA onset detection sits near F1 0.88 across datasets; SuperFlux and CNN detectors perform comparably.
findings.implication: Audio-derived onset error ships with a detector-confidence caveat and never overrides the MIDI-truth gate.

findings.title: SwiftF0: Fast and Accurate Monophonic Pitch Detection
findings.finding: SwiftF0 operates on the magnitude spectrogram, 91.8% harmonic mean at 10 dB SNR, 95,842 params, ~42x CREPE CPU speed.
findings.implication: A spectrogram-derived pitch is legitimate when a trained model reads it; peak-picking a mel plot is not a substitute.

findings.title: RMVPE: A Robust Model for Vocal Pitch Estimation in Polyphonic Music
findings.finding: RMVPE extracts vocal pitch from polyphonic mixes without separation, stable across SNR.
findings.implication: Route pitch through RMVPE when the reference is a produced mix.

findings.title: Pitch-and-Spectrum-Aware Singing Quality Assessment with Bias Correction and Model Fusion
findings.finding: The winning VoiceMOS 2024 singing predictor reaches utterance-level SRCC 0.639 (system-level 0.888).
findings.implication: Aggregate across takes before any comparative claim.

findings.title: essentia.js - npm registry metadata
findings.finding: essentia.js is AGPL-3.0 and last published 2021-06-24.
findings.implication: Excluded: AGPL in the tree of an MIT npm package.

findings.title: Meyda audio features / npm 5.6.3
findings.finding: Meyda is MIT with offline extraction, MFCC and chroma but no raw mel bands; last release 2024-04-21.
findings.implication: Usable for spectral scalars; the mel filterbank is still ours to write.

findings.title: TensorFlow.js API signal namespace; fft.js npm
findings.finding: tfjs ships stft/frame/hannWindow but no mel filterbank op; fft.js is a MIT radix-4 FFT.
findings.implication: Skip the tensor runtime; take the FFT from fft.js and write ~200 lines of DSP.

findings.title: Web Audio API 1.1 s1.8.5-1.8.6 AnalyserNode
findings.finding: AnalyserNode mandates a Blackman window, 0.8 default smoothing, and reads only the most recent fftSize frames (max 32768).
findings.implication: AnalyserNode is excluded from the analysis path; compute the STFT over the rendered AudioBuffer.

findings.title: librosa.filters.mel vs torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram defaults
findings.finding: librosa's mel default is htk=False, norm='slaney'; torchaudio's is mel_scale='htk', norm=None.
findings.implication: Expose melScale and norm explicitly in the tool schema and pin them.

findings.title: MelSpectrogram inconsistency with librosa melspectrogram (pytorch/audio #1058)
findings.finding: The librosa/torchaudio mel mismatch is a filed real-world bug class.
findings.implication: Pick one reference (pinned librosa) and generate goldens from it.

findings.title: whisper/audio.py log_mel_spectrogram
findings.finding: Whisper's log-mel uses Hann/n_fft 400/hop 160, power, log10, a peak-relative clamp at max-8, then (x+4)/4.
findings.implication: Peak-relative dB changes every value when a clip is trimmed; record ref explicitly.

findings.title: librosa.power_to_db (0.11)
findings.finding: power_to_db defaults ref=1.0, amin=1e-10, top_db=80.
findings.implication: Tests use ref=1.0, top_db=null; peak-relative dB is display-only.

findings.title: MIT JS building blocks for mel and CQT
findings.finding: meljs 1.0.2 (NeMo-calibrated mel), cqt-web 1.0.4 (librosa-compatible CQT, WASM), wavedraw 2.7.0 (Node WAV + mel render) are all MIT.
findings.implication: Read as reference implementations; meljs's NeMo constants would break librosa parity if vendored unchecked.

findings.title: audio-analysis-mcp
findings.finding: An existing audio-analysis MCP server (librosa + matplotlib) saves visual outputs to disk and returns paths.
findings.implication: Precedent for path + numbers; match this repo's view_scored_piano_roll shape (path + inline image + summary).

findings.title: OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob(); pngjs 7.0.0; sharp 0.35.4
findings.finding: convertToBlob produces PNG in every browser and in Workers; pngjs is pure-JS MIT; sharp is a native binary.
findings.implication: Raster PNG is the render target; a 30 s clip at 10 ms hop is 384,000 cells, so rect-per-cell SVG is out.
